question: Explain whether merchandise sales changed mainly because of order volume or average merchandise per order. If sales declined, drill down by category and seller.

evidence.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-11-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2017-12-01') THEN o.order_id END) AS baseline_orders, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-11-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2017-12-01') THEN COALESCE(i.price,0) ELSE 0 END),2) AS baseline_sales, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-12-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01') THEN o.order_id END) AS target_orders, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-12-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01') THEN COALESCE(i.price,0) ELSE 0 END),2) AS target_sales FROM orders o LEFT JOIN order_items i ON o.order_id=i.order_id WHERE (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-11-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2017-12-01') OR (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-12-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01')

SELECT p.product_category_name AS dimension_key, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-12-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01') THEN o.order_id END) - COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-11-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2017-12-01') THEN o.order_id END) AS change_value FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON i.order_id=o.order_id LEFT JOIN products p ON i.product_id=p.product_id WHERE ((o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-11-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2017-12-01') OR (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-12-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01')) GROUP BY p.product_category_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-12-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01') THEN o.order_id END) - COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-11-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2017-12-01') THEN o.order_id END) < 0 ORDER BY change_value, p.product_category_name NULLS LAST LIMIT 5

SELECT i.seller_id AS dimension_key, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-12-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01') THEN o.order_id END) - COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-11-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2017-12-01') THEN o.order_id END) AS change_value FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ON i.order_id=o.order_id LEFT JOIN products p ON i.product_id=p.product_id WHERE ((o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-11-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2017-12-01') OR (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-12-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01')) AND p.product_category_name = 'cama_mesa_banho' GROUP BY i.seller_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-12-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01') THEN o.order_id END) - COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN (o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-11-01' AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2017-12-01') THEN o.order_id END) < 0 ORDER BY change_value, i.seller_id NULLS LAST LIMIT 5

decisions.reason: Need to decompose the merchandise sales change between 2017-11 and 2017-12 into order volume versus average merchandise per order drivers before deciding on further category/seller drill-down.

Sales declined month-over-month (1,010,271.37 to 743,914.17) alongside a drop in orders (7,544 to 5,673). Because the observed change is negative, the question asks to drill down by category; category_order_declines ranks categories by decline in distinct orders, which identifies category-level volume contributions to the decline.

Sales declined from 1,010,271.37 to 743,914.17, driven mainly by orders falling from 7,544 to 5,673; the leading declining category is cama_mesa_banho (-336 orders), so the next step is to rank seller order-count declines within that category.
